'''Matt Dillahunty''' is an American atheist activist and debater, best known as a long-running host of '''''The Atheist Experience''''', the Austin-based public-access call-in show, and as a fixture of the atheism-versus-apologetics debate circuit that overlapped the [[The Great Debate Era|Great Debate]] years. He appears in [[Media and Personalities]] as an arena entry — covered for how he argues.

== Who he is ==

Raised a fundamentalist Christian and once headed toward ministry, Dillahunty set out to prove his faith, concluded it did not hold up, and became one of the more visible public atheists of the YouTube era. His platform is the live call-in debate: believers phone in, and he presses them on '''why they believe what they believe'''.

== What he argues ==

His method is epistemology first. He foregrounds the '''burden of proof''' (the claimant must support the claim, not the skeptic disprove it), the distinction between knowledge and belief, and the difference between being convinced by evidence and wanting something to be true. He is closely associated with '''street epistemology'''–style questioning: rather than refuting a conclusion, he probes how the person arrived at it.

== The strong case ==

He is clear, patient, and genuinely good at the thing he does — making abstract points about evidence and reasoning legible to a caller with no philosophy background, in real time. His consistency on burden of proof and his refusal to let a conversation skip past its premises are a real public-education service, whatever one's own beliefs.

== The weak case ==

Critics — including sympathetic ones — note that the format rewards a combative, sometimes dismissive style, that the same moves recur against weaker and stronger interlocutors alike, and that "I'm not convinced" can function as a conversation-stopper as easily as a rigorous stance. He is strongest against sloppy argument and less interesting against serious ones.
